title: Ultrashort Two-Pulse Train Generation on a 100 TW Laser Beamline Using a Delay Mask After the Final Focusing Optics
abstract: Experimental results showing the generation of an ultrashort two-pulse train using a two-section delay mask placed downstream of the off-axis parabola focusing optics are reported. Based on the initial simulation results, a circular fused silica plate with a central aperture and a measured thickness of $570\pm50$ $μ$m used in the quantitative delay calculation was designed to enable two distinct transverse portions of the incident laser pulse to be focused, ideally, with equal intensity. This fulfills one of the requirements of the resonant multi-pulse ionization injection (ReMPI) scheme for laser wakefield acceleration. As an intermediary step, a calibration of Gafchromic EBT4 films against laser fluence was established, enabling direct characterization of the unattenuated transverse beam profile. The experiment was carried out at the CNR-INO Intense Laser Irradiation Laboratory (ILIL) using a 240 TW laser system operated at 100 TW as part of the ongoing preparation for the first experimental demonstration of ReMPI. The pulse-to-pulse delay introduced by the delay mask was experimentally measured (at a reduced power, as customary for temporal autocorrelation measurements) to be $\simeq 901$ fs, in good agreement with the expected value of $\simeq 888$ fs. While the pulse-to-pulse delay is not yet optimized for ReMPI operation at practically relevant plasma densities, the experimental results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed delay-mask concept.
